key_insight: Combining 3D welding simulations with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection for reducing weld defects, thermal gradients and axial-force fluctuations in HDPE joints.
method: Simulate temperature, force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force responses.
Combine simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good CEL agreement, ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99, and a peak plunge-force reduction from 1600 N to about 1100 N with 60 °C preheating.
watch_item: Predictive performance beyond the tested process-parameter range remains unestablished and requires further validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
